chapter: Kline 1980: early years and founding of the Goldkette orchestra
title: How the Goldkette orchestra and Graystone Ballroom were founded
summary: Virginia tells how her father discovered Goldkette playing in Chicago silent movie houses, and how they and Doc Ryker formed the original Goldkette orchestra around the Graystone Ballroom in Detroit.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional

blocks.x: Well, I don't know how you would call a feel for it (we have to go over this tape because it's going to be pretty awful). If you guide my hand in the recall now...Jean Gene Goldkette left Chicago. He was a very young fellow. He had left Chicago because this job came up for him in Detroit, Michigan. And he left Chicago out from under the wing of my father you might say.
And why your father? Why was your father involved?
My father was the one who discovered Jean Goldkette, who was playing in the silent movies. They were called the nickel show at that time.

And he took him under his wing and got him different jobs in Chicago until he became a quite well-known pianist, and played in these lovely clubs. Like they had a very classy club in Chicago, some....

He got in there. Jean acquired this position with the Detroit Athletic Club in Detroit. And then he left there. It seemed there was some correspondence between my father and Jean and my brother Charles. And Jean was the one who told my brother Charlie and my father about the Greystone Ballroom building which was actually a Chinese Restaurant, I think it was originally. And this building was available at a very good price.
Was he looking for a place?

And they were planning to form an orchestra and have a ballroom too for this orchestra to play in. So like musicians do, they picked out all these fellows and got them together which Doc Ryker was one of the very original of the Goldkette band. He was one of the original people. And they formed this band and decided to
use Jean's name. Jean tried to direct it.
He tried to direct it but he was unsuccessful. He didn't understand jazz that well. This might be a blow.
For the piano arrangement, Jean couldn't play it.

He couldn't play jazz. He was strictly a classical man. So therefore he became on the business end of the formation of the original Jean Goldkette orchestra. And my brother and my father moved to Detroit. And the whole family moved to Detroit.
Where were they living before then?
And this first orchestra was - the original Jean Goldkette orchestra was formed.
But they made their first record in early '24. So it would be before then.
That's another...and maybe in Doc Ryker's article there, he would have the information.
Maybe I have better recall on that.
